# Brief 1.2: audio engine, click track, pointer input

**Goal.** The production clock and sound for the duel, and the single pointer-input path. The whole game is timed from the clock you build here, so its behaviour must be exact and monotonic. This runs in parallel with the core rules task; you depend only on the `Clock` type.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md` (timing rules), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `src/core/types.ts` (do not edit).

**Files you own (create):** `src/audio/engine.ts`, `src/audio/click.ts`, `src/audio/sfx.ts`, `src/input/pointer.ts`, `tests/unit/click.test.ts`, `tests/unit/pointer.test.ts`, `tests/unit/audioclock.test.ts`. Touch nothing else (another agent is working in `src/core/` and `tests/unit/duel*.ts`, `beat*.ts`, `tunables*.ts` at the same time). Add no dependencies.

## The clock model

The game's `Clock` is **heard time**: the position on the audio timeline that is coming out of the speakers now. `heard = context.currentTime - latency`, where `latency` is `context.outputLatency || context.baseLatency || 0`, read once when playback is armed (`resume()`) and then held fixed so the clock stays monotonic. To make something audible at clock time `T`, schedule it at context time `T + latency`.

`context.currentTime` advances in steps of a render quantum (about 3 ms), so interpolate inside a quantum with `performance.now()`: remember the `(contextTime, performanceTime)` pair each time `currentTime` is seen to change, return `contextTime + elapsed`, capped at one quantum ahead, and never return less than the previous value. This interpolation and `timeOfEvent` are the only permitted uses of `performance.now()` for timing in the project; comment them as such.

## Interfaces

```ts
// src/audio/engine.ts
import type { Clock } from '../core/types';

/** Pure, testable core of the clock. `readContextTime` and `readPerfMs` are injected. */
export class AudioClock implements Clock {
  constructor(readContextTime: () => number, readPerfMs: () => number, quantumSec?: number);
  latencySec: number; // settable; default 0
  now(): number; // heard time, seconds, monotonic
  /** Clock time at which a DOM event with this `event.timeStamp` (performance ms) happened. */
  timeOfEvent(timeStampMs: number): number;
  /** Context time at which to schedule audio so it is heard at clock time `t`. */
  toContextTime(t: number): number;
}

export interface PlayHandle {
  stop(atClockTime?: number): void;
}

export interface LoopOptions {
  /** Clock time at which buffer position `offset` should be heard. */
  startTime: number;
  /** Seconds into the buffer that correspond to `startTime` (the first beat). Default 0. */
  offset?: number;
  /** Loop region in buffer seconds. Default: offset .. buffer.duration. */
  loopStart?: number;
  loopEnd?: number;
  gain?: number;
}

export class AudioEngine {
  constructor(); // must not throw when constructed before a user gesture
  readonly context: AudioContext;
  readonly clock: AudioClock;
  /** Call from a user gesture. Resumes the context and fixes the latency value. */
  resume(): Promise<void>;
  readonly running: boolean;
  decode(data: ArrayBuffer): Promise<AudioBuffer>;
  /** Start a looping buffer. If `startTime` is already in the past, start now at the matching position inside the loop so the beat stays aligned. */
  playLoop(buffer: AudioBuffer, opts: LoopOptions): PlayHandle;
  /** One-shot, e.g. a metronome tick or sound effect, heard at clock time `when` (default: as soon as possible). */
  playOnce(buffer: AudioBuffer, when?: number, gain?: number): PlayHandle;
  setMusicVolume(v: number): void; // 0..1, music bus (loops)
  setSfxVolume(v: number): void; // 0..1, effects bus (one-shots)
  stopAll(): void;
}
```

```ts
// src/audio/click.ts
export interface ClickTrackSpec {
  bpm: number;
  beats: number; // loop length in beats
  sampleRate: number;
  beatsPerBar?: number; // accent every N beats; default 4
}
/** Pure sample generator (mono Float32Array), usable in Node tests. Length = ceil(beats * 60/bpm * sampleRate) plus a short tail so the loop end can be set exactly. */
export function renderClickTrack(spec: ClickTrackSpec): Float32Array;
/** Exact loop length in seconds: beats * 60 / bpm. */
export function clickLoopSeconds(spec: Pick<ClickTrackSpec, 'bpm' | 'beats'>): number;
/** `beats` defaults to 16. */
export function createClickBuffer(ctx: BaseAudioContext, bpm: number, beats?: number): AudioBuffer;
```

The click track is the test song, so make it pleasant enough to play to: a low kick on every beat, a quieter closed-hat tick on every half-beat, a brighter accent on the first beat of each bar, and a simple two-note bass pulse. Everything is synthesised with sines, noise bursts from a seeded deterministic generator (no `Math.random`) and exponential decays. Every onset must begin exactly at its beat's sample index (`round(beatIndex * 60/bpm * sampleRate)`). Sounds that would cross the loop end must wrap around to the start so the loop is seamless. Peak amplitude at most 0.9.

```ts
// src/audio/sfx.ts
export type SfxName = 'plant' | 'bravo' | 'good' | 'miss' | 'tick' | 'actOver';
/** Short synthesised effects, built once per engine and cached. `when` is clock time; default: now. */
export function createSfx(engine: AudioEngine): { play(name: SfxName, when?: number): void };
```

```ts
// src/input/pointer.ts
import type { Clock } from '../core/types';
export interface Rect {
  left: number;
  top: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}
export interface PointerSample {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  inside: boolean;
  touch: boolean;
  down: boolean;
}
export interface PointerClick extends PointerSample {
  time: number; // clock seconds
}
/** Pure: client pixels to play-area fractions. x and y are NOT clamped; `inside` says whether 0<=x<=1 and 0<=y<=1. */
export function toPlayArea(
  clientX: number,
  clientY: number,
  rect: Rect,
): { x: number; y: number; inside: boolean };
export interface PointerInputOptions {
  element: HTMLElement;
  /** AudioClock satisfies this. */
  clock: Clock & { timeOfEvent?(timeStampMs: number): number };
  /** Play area in client pixels, read on every event (it changes on resize). */
  getPlayRect(): Rect;
  onMove?(s: PointerSample): void;
  onDown?(c: PointerClick): void;
  onUp?(s: PointerSample): void;
}
/** Attaches pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup and pointercancel listeners. Returns a detach function. */
export function attachPointerInput(opts: PointerInputOptions): () => void;
```

Pointer rules: Pointer Events only (no mouse or touch events). Only the primary pointer counts, and for a mouse only the primary button is a click. `touch` is `event.pointerType === 'touch'` (a pen is not touch). Use `clock.timeOfEvent(event.timeStamp)` when available, else `clock.now()`. Call `preventDefault` on a touch pointerdown so no synthetic mouse events or scrolling follow, and set `touch-action: none` on the element (restore the old value on detach).

## Tests (Vitest, node environment; there is no real AudioContext)

- `audioclock.test.ts`, with injected readers: `now()` subtracts latency; interpolates between context steps; never goes backwards when the context time stalls or the perf reader jitters; is capped at one quantum past the last seen context time; `toContextTime` adds latency; `timeOfEvent` maps an older timestamp to an earlier clock time.
- `click.test.ts`: buffer length; peak <= 0.9; no NaN; energy in the 5 ms after each beat onset is far higher than in the 5 ms before it; two renders are identical; `clickLoopSeconds` exact.
- `pointer.test.ts`: `toPlayArea` centre, corners, outside, and a zero-size rect gives `inside: false` with no NaN.

`AudioEngine`, `createSfx` and `attachPointerInput` need a browser; keep them thin and say in your report that they are untested here.
